', '# =============================================================================
# ✅  ENGINEER-SIGNED-OFF (Kiran Nayak, 2026-07-13). Values verified against the
#    PCF8574/PCF8574A + HD44780U datasheets and a real module (I2C-scanned).
#
# NOTES (the values a generic LLM gets wrong):
#   - i2c_address 0x27 / alt 0x3F: the base address is set by the I/O-expander part.
#     PCF8574 backpack → 0x27; PCF8574A backpack → 0x3F. A0-A2 solder jumpers shift
#     it (PCF8574: 0x20-0x27, PCF8574A: 0x38-0x3F). CONFIRM with an I2C bus scan.
#   - voltage / logic_level 5.0: most 1602 backpacks are 5V parts. Some newer boards
#     are 3V3-tolerant — CONFIRM the specific module before trusting the 5V value.
#   - library: LiquidCrystal_I2C is the arduino-esp32 convention (framework choice,
#     not a datasheet fact) — confirm it is the one your generator targets.
#
# Composition (ADR-041): class:[display, i2c_device] pulls in BOTH rule-packs —
#   i2c        → requires i2c_address, blocks out-of-range addresses, bus failure modes
#   display    → init-before-write obligations
# =============================================================================

class: [display, i2c_device]      # composition — this part IS both (playbook §10)
interface: i2c

i2c_address: 0x27                 # PCF8574 backpack default (7-bit)
alt_i2c_address: 0x3F             # PCF8574A backpack variant
voltage: 5.0                      # module supply
logic_level: 5.0                  # 5V logic vs 3V3 ESP32 I2C — a real constraint (see quirks)
pullups_required: true            # backpacks usually carry their own SDA/SCL pull-ups
library: "LiquidCrystal_I2C"      # arduino-esp32 framework convention (not a datasheet fact)

codegen_obligations:
  - "init: lcd.init() (or lcd.begin(16,2)); then lcd.backlight()"

# Device-specific pitfalls (playbook §5.2 — optional `quirks`, your judgment).
# These are advisory grounding, NOT closed-shape constraints.
quirks:
  - "Address is module-dependent: PCF8574 boards default 0x27, PCF8574A boards 0x3F; A0-A2 jumpers shift it. Always I2C-scan a new module rather than assuming."
  - "Contrast is set by the blue trimpot on the backpack. If it is not adjusted the glass shows a blank line or a row of solid boxes even when wiring and code are correct — a classic 'it doesn't work' that is not a firmware bug."
  - "5V part on a 3V3 ESP32: the backpack pulls SDA/SCL up toward 5V, which exceeds the ESP32's input voltage spec. It often 'works on the bench' but a bidirectional level shifter is the correct fix for a production design."

# ✅  ENGINEER-SIGNED-OFF (Kiran Nayak, 2026-07-15). Sensor-role conventions reviewed.
#
# The `sensor` functional-role class carries ONLY what is common to ALL sensors
# (I2C, SPI, analog, single-wire). A sensor's addressing/interface comes from its
# BUS class (i2c_device / spi_device) or from being wired to a plain GPIO/ADC —
# NOT from being a sensor. So `properties` is minimal on purpose.
#
# COUNTEREXAMPLE GATE (playbook §10): every rule below must survive I2C (BME280),
# SPI, analog (LDR/thermistor), and single-wire (DHT22) members.
#   - `min_read_interval_ms` is OPTIONAL, not required — a streaming/continuous
#     sensor simply omits it. Making it required would break those members.
#   - No universal closed-shape validation exists across all sensor interfaces,
#     so `validations` is empty (per §9.1, only closed shapes are hard blocks).
# =============================================================================

applies_to: [sensor]

# period declares it here (e.g. DHT22 = 2000); continuous sensors omit it.

validations: []

  - "validate the reading (range / error flag) before using it downstream"

# ✅  ENGINEER-SIGNED-OFF (Kiran Nayak, 2026-07-13). Display-class conventions
#    reviewed against HD44780 / SSD1306 / ST7789 / LTDC / e-paper behaviour.
#
# The `display` class carries ONLY what is genuinely common to ALL display
# controllers (HD44780 char LCDs, SSD1306 OLEDs, ST7789 TFTs, LTDC/RGB panels,
# e-paper). A display's ADDRESSING / interface obligations come from its BUS class
# (`i2c_device` / `spi_device`) — so `properties` is empty on purpose.
#
# COUNTEREXAMPLE GATE (playbook §10): a rule earns a place here only if it survives
# every member type. Deliberately KEPT OUT because they fail on some member:
#   - "clear the display RAM / set the cursor before writing" — false for HD44780
#     (no pre-clear needed), SSD1306 (page-addressed, not a cursor), ST7789
#     (window + RAMWR, no char cursor), LTDC/RGB (no controller RAM), e-paper
#     (clearing = flicker + long refresh). → device-level, not the class.
#   - "garbled output" causes (pixel format, window, endianness, RGB/BGR, timing)
#     are interface/device-specific. → device / interface-binding record.
# The rich display ontology (transport / interface_binding / device_protocol /
# addressing_model / rendering_model) and a symptom→cause→check→action diagnostic
# schema are DEFERRED (playbook §3.2 register; Layer-6 `failures/`).
# =============================================================================

applies_to: [display]

# No property is required of ALL displays; bus classes supply address/CS/mode.
properties: {}

# No universal closed-shape constraint applies to every display type.
validations: []

# Advisory grounding, inherited by every display device. Kept universal on purpose:
# it names a symptom CATEGORY and points at diagnosis rather than prescribing a remedy.
failure_modes:
  - {condition: "no visible output after startup",
     handling: "diagnose the cause (power, reset level, controller init, bus/address, backlight or contrast) before assuming a re-init is the fix",

codegen_obligations:
  - "initialise the display controller (per its device-specific init sequence) before the first write"

', '# =============================================================================
# ✅  ENGINEER-SIGNED-OFF (Kiran Nayak, 2026-07-15). Sensor-role conventions reviewed.
#
# The `sensor` functional-role class carries ONLY what is common to ALL sensors
# (I2C, SPI, analog, single-wire). A sensor's addressing/interface comes from its
# BUS class (i2c_device / spi_device) or from being wired to a plain GPIO/ADC —
# NOT from being a sensor. So `properties` is minimal on purpose.
#
# COUNTEREXAMPLE GATE (playbook §10): every rule below must survive I2C (BME280),
# SPI, analog (LDR/thermistor), and single-wire (DHT22) members.
#   - `min_read_interval_ms` is OPTIONAL, not required — a streaming/continuous
#     sensor simply omits it. Making it required would break those members.
#   - No universal closed-shape validation exists across all sensor interfaces,
#     so `validations` is empty (per §9.1, only closed shapes are hard blocks).
# =============================================================================

class: sensor
applies_to: [sensor]

# Optional, recognised sensor property. A device that has a minimum sampling
# period declares it here (e.g. DHT22 = 2000); continuous sensors omit it.
properties:
  min_read_interval_ms: {type: int, required: false}

validations: []

# Advisory grounding, inherited by every sensor device.
failure_modes:
  - {condition: "stale, out-of-range, or error reading",
     handling: "range-check / validate a reading before using it; don't propagate a bad sample",
     severity: recommendation}

codegen_obligations:
  - "if the device declares min_read_interval_ms, do not sample faster than it"
  - "validate the reading (range / error flag) before using it downstream"

#   i2c        → requires i2c_address, blocks out-of-range addresses, bus failure modes
#   display    → init-before-write obligations
# =============================================================================

class: [display, i2c_device]      # composition — this part IS both (playbook §10)
interface: i2c

i2c_address: 0x27                 # PCF8574 backpack default (7-bit)
alt_i2c_address: 0x3F             # PCF8574A backpack variant
voltage: 5.0                      # module supply
logic_level: 5.0                  # 5V logic vs 3V3 ESP32 I2C — a real constraint (see quirks)
pullups_required: true            # backpacks usually carry their own SDA/SCL pull-ups
library: "LiquidCrystal_I2C"      # arduino-esp32 framework convention (not a datasheet fact)

  - {gpio: 32, input_only: false, adc: "ADC1_CH4", pwm: true,  strapping: false}   # Table3 pin8 — XTAL_32K_P, TOUCH9
  - {gpio: 33, input_only: false, adc: "ADC1_CH5", pwm: true,  strapping: false}   # Table3 pin9 — XTAL_32K_N, TOUCH8

  - {gpio: 35, input_only: true,  adc: "ADC1_CH7", pwm: false, strapping: false,

  - {gpio: 36, input_only: true,  adc: "ADC1_CH0", pwm: false, strapping: false,

#   - voltage / logic_level 5.0: most 1602 backpacks are 5V parts. Some newer boards
#     are 3V3-tolerant — CONFIRM the specific module before trusting the 5V value.
#   - library: LiquidCrystal_I2C is the arduino-esp32 convention (framework choice,
#     not a datasheet fact) — confirm it is the one your generator targets.
#
# Composition (ADR-041): class:[display, i2c_device] pulls in BOTH rule-packs —
#   i2c        → requires i2c_address, blocks out-of-range addresses, bus failure modes
#   display    → init-before-write obligations
# =============================================================================

class: [display, i2c_device]      # composition — this part IS both (playbook §10)
interface: i2c

i2c_address: 0x27                 # PCF8574 backpack default (7-bit)
alt_i2c_address: 0x3F             # PCF8574A backpack variant
voltage: 5.0                      # module supply
logic_level: 5.0                  # 5V logic vs 3V3 ESP32 I2C — a real constraint (see quirks)
pullups_required: true            # backpacks usually carry their own SDA/SCL pull-ups
library: "LiquidCrystal_I2C"      # arduino-esp32 framework convention (not a datasheet fact)

codegen_obligations:
  - "init: lcd.init() (or lcd.begin(16,2)); then lcd.backlight()"

# These are advisory grounding, NOT closed-shape constraints.
quirks:
  - "Address is module-dependent: PCF8574 boards default 0x27, PCF8574A boards 0x3F; A0-A2 jumpers shift it. Always I2C-scan a new module rather than assuming."
  - "Contrast is set by the blue trimpot on the backpack. If it is not adjusted the glass shows a blank line or a row of solid boxes even when wiring and code are correct — a classic 'it doesn't work' that is not a firmware bug."
  - "5V part on a 3V3 ESP32: the backpack pulls SDA/SCL up toward 5V, which exceeds the ESP32's input voltage spec. It often 'works on the bench' but a bidirectional level shifter is the correct fix for a production design."

# ✅  ENGINEER-SIGNED-OFF (Kiran Nayak, 2026-07-13). Display-class conventions
#    reviewed against HD44780 / SSD1306 / ST7789 / LTDC / e-paper behaviour.
#
# The `display` class carries ONLY what is genuinely common to ALL display
# controllers (HD44780 char LCDs, SSD1306 OLEDs, ST7789 TFTs, LTDC/RGB panels,
# e-paper). A display's ADDRESSING / interface obligations come from its BUS class
# (`i2c_device` / `spi_device`) — so `properties` is empty on purpose.
#
# COUNTEREXAMPLE GATE (playbook §10): a rule earns a place here only if it survives
# every member type. Deliberately KEPT OUT because they fail on some member:
#   - "clear the display RAM / set the cursor before writing" — false for HD44780
#     (no pre-clear needed), SSD1306 (page-addressed, not a cursor), ST7789
#     (window + RAMWR, no char cursor), LTDC/RGB (no controller RAM), e-paper
#     (clearing = flicker + long refresh). → device-level, not the class.
#   - "garbled output" causes (pixel format, window, endianness, RGB/BGR, timing)
#     are interface/device-specific. → device / interface-binding record.
# The rich display ontology (transport / interface_binding / device_protocol /
# addressing_model / rendering_model) and a symptom→cause→check→action diagnostic
# schema are DEFERRED (playbook §3.2 register; Layer-6 `failures/`).
# =============================================================================

class: display
applies_to: [display]

# No property is required of ALL displays; bus classes supply address/CS/mode.
properties: {}

# No universal closed-shape constraint applies to every display type.
validations: []

# Advisory grounding, inherited by every display device. Kept universal on purpose:
# it names a symptom CATEGORY and points at diagnosis rather than prescribing a remedy.
failure_modes:
  - {condition: "no visible output after startup",
     handling: "diagnose the cause (power, reset level, controller init, bus/address, backlight or contrast) before assuming a re-init is the fix",
     severity: recommendation}

codegen_obligations:
  - "initialise the display controller (per its device-specific init sequence) before the first write"

#

# (I2C, SPI, analog, single-wire). A sensor's addressing/interface comes from its
